analysis:
I examined the base text of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1-1178) together with the complete patch excerpt.

The head adds stored state at head lines 705-716:
- selectedModelRecovery (SelectedModelRecovery).
- selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride, a test seam that is nil in production.
- savedEnabledModels.
- enabledModelsAtLastSwitch.

Head line 868 initializes savedEnabledModels from config.config.backend.enabledModels.

This file only declares the new state. The new state does not touch:
- keyPair or signer creation (base 895-897).
- Attestation, binary or weight hashes (modelHashes/liveModelHashes).
- Advertised-model filtering (base 876-893).
- KV budget or prefix-cache paths (T-041).

No security regression is visible here.

Integration must examine ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, which is not supplied. It should verify that:
- Recovery loads only advertised, eligible models with a verified weight hash and self-test, honoring retiringModels and failedSelfTestHashes so a failed build is not reloaded (an ABA risk; relates to T-012/T-027).
- The no-eviction recovery load respects the memory gate and drain/update/shutdown admission barriers (availability).
- The production path never sets the test override.
- savedEnabledModels, which is read from an operator-writable config file, influences only status reporting and not serving selection or advertisement without a committed switch (TB-003, T-013).
